Real-time news, insights, prices, trending stories, and expert analysis - all in one place.OpenAI and Meta Join Forces, Bridging the "Last Mile" of Agent CommerceOn November 13, 2026, two major announcements landed the same day, together addressing the "last mile" of agent commerce: how AI assistants get through the door, and how they pay.

Sierra and Meta released Poppy v1.0, a Personal Agent Protocol built on OAuth, HTTPS, OpenAPI, and the Model Context Protocol. Poppy lets businesses cryptographically verify three things: which assistant is making a request, which user it represents, and what permissions it holds. Companies publish a discovery file at /.well-known/poppy describing endpoints and allowed actions, while both user and business must consent to each interaction via two-way authorization. Shopify automatically enabled Poppy discovery files for merchants in 175+ countries, giving the protocol immediate scale, with over 100 design partners including Delta, 1Password, Okta, and Cloudflare.

Separately, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet for its personal assistant dots. The assistant can search, compare, and fill a cart, but must stop at checkout—users confirm via biometric authentication. Neither the assistant nor the merchant ever sees the real card number; card networks issue a one-time payment credential instead. Built with Amex, Mastercard, and Visa, the wallet runs entirely on traditional fiat rails—explicitly not crypto or stablecoins. It initially opens only to US Pro subscribers aged 18+.

Notably, Visa and Mastercard span both initiatives, and OpenAI itself appears among Poppy's design partners—despite dots and Meta's Muse competing for the consumer entry point. The shared logic: consumer-facing competition, but shared infrastructure on the business side.
